biggest_gap: When the wanted clip is not the latest (the booking link, an older email or phone, the address, the JD link), the losing side makes the person dig: either ⌘Space ⌘4 and type a search (~4.19 s, five keystroke groups) or ⌘V then trim×4 (~2.75 s), where the other side lands the right text with one hotkey press and a number (~1.9-3.2 s). The person has to know a search term, type it, and pick the row themselves.
notes: The two sides are identical on 33 of 46 steps (plain ⌘V, 0.28 s). The gaps all sit in the 'clip is not the latest' steps. On those, hotkey-plus-number is 1.9-2.2 s when it works, but it is not consistently the faster side: steps 23 and 25 show one side needing trim×4 (2.75 s) and a 6.66 s Spotlight+trim, and steps 10, 30, 32, 36 show the other side doing a 4.19 s Spotlight search. Neither side reaches ⌘V-speed on any of these, and the hotkey path still costs the person a number lookup or a typed filter (steps 36, 39, 44, 45 still need type:xxx). Waits of 268-285 ms on the hotkey (steps 21, 23, 25) sit right at the noticeable edge, and 158 ms at step 44. Step 25 is the worst moment in the day for both: 4.67 s at best for a phone number. Steps 27 (password field) and 41/42 (identical prep emails, same address landed twice) are the same on both sides, so nothing separates them; the second prep email landing the same candidate both times is correct only because order was declared not to matter.
